what: Published bilinear-complexity bounds for polynomial multiplication over F2, as they stand in the literature. Every row is transcribed from a named source and is NOT a result of this repository; what this repository computes goes in certs/bilinear-certificate.json and is compared against these.
convention: P_n, T_n, C_n multiply two polynomials of n coefficients each (degree n-1). P is the full product (2n-1 coefficients out), T the truncated/short product (the low n coefficients), C the cyclic product modulo X^n - 1. Over F2, X^n + 1 = X^n - 1, so the negacyclic product C_n^- IS C_n and carries no separate row.
lowerBoundSource: Chengu Wang, 'Automated Lower Bounds for Bilinear Complexity over Finite Fields', arXiv:2603.07280. The 'previous' column is the best lower bound before that paper, as Wang's Table 1 reports it.

refs.26: P. L. Montgomery, 'Five, six, and seven-term Karatsuba-like formulae', IEEE Trans. Computers 54(3):362-369, 2005
refs.27: S. D. Morgera, 'Multiplicative complexity of bilinear algorithms for cyclic convolution over finite fields', Multidimensional Systems and Signal Processing 1(1):99-111, 1990
refs.32: M. D. Wagh and S. D. Morgera, 'A new structured design method for convolutions over finite fields, part I', IEEE Trans. Information Theory 29(4):583-595, 1983
refs.34: S. Winograd, 'Some bilinear forms whose multiplicative complexity depends on the field of constants', Mathematical Systems Theory 10(2):169-180, 1977
refs.CK25: S. Chen and M. Kauers, 'Flip Graphs for Polynomial Multiplication', arXiv:2502.06264, February 2025 - flip-graph search over Z2 for the FULL product only
refs.W-fn: Wang, arXiv:2603.07280, footnote to Table 1: a new upper bound of 26 for multiplication over Z[x]/x^9, obtained by flip-graph search over F2 and lifted to Z

rows.upperNote: TIGHT: the lower and upper bounds meet, so 13 is the exact rank

Wang's Table 1 cites 27 from [12] and then improves it to 26 himself, in a footnote, BY FLIP-GRAPH SEARCH OVER F2 - the only truncated case modern search has been pointed at. 26 is the number to beat.

chenKauersFullProduct.what: Chen & Kauers ran the SAME method this repository uses - a flip graph over F2 - on the FULL product, and published a table over Z2. These are their square-case ranks, which this repository uses as a calibration ladder: a walk that cannot reach them is a walk whose numbers elsewhere mean nothing.
chenKauersFullProduct.note: Their P6, P7, P8 land exactly ON the Montgomery/Winograd-Fan-Hasan upper bounds above, never below. They do not touch the cyclic, truncated or negacyclic families - those words do not appear in the paper.
